content.title: Artemis II: Exploring Our Return to the Moon
content.text: For over 50 years, humans have looked at the Moon from a distance, wondering when we’d return. Now, the countdown is on! NASA’s Artemis II mission is expected to launch in April, carrying astronauts farther from Earth than any crew has traveled since the Apollo era. Building on the success of the Artemis I mission, Artemis II will send four astronauts on an approximately 10-day mission around the Moon demonstrating a broad range of capabilities needed for deep space missions. *Launch timing is subject to change due to mission readiness, weather, and technical reviews. The Cox Science Center and Aquarium is now streaming NASA+ and will have live coverage Artemis II as it continues its journey around the moon. We will also stream the documentary "Moonbound" with timed shows in our observatory. Moonbound explores the physical and mental challenges of preparing for a crewed flight around the Moon, and the teamwork required to test new systems at the edge of exploration. Moonbound Showtimes: Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Saturdays 1 p.m., 2 p.m., 3 p.m. and 4 p.m. (11am & 12pm on April 1st Launch Day) On Apr 1, the Cox Science Center and Aquarium will provide fun space-themed activations throughout including: Moon Painting VR Space Mission (Saturday) Moon Sand Play Observing the Lunar reconnaissance orbiter (LRO) STEAM Cart Activities including constellations and Mars Helicopter Craft Glazer Hall and Cox Science Center and Aquarium's Science Film Series The Cox Science Center and Aquarium is partnering with Glazer Hall to present a monthly film series that brings the wonder of real science to the big screen. Designed for audiences of all ages, the series invites guests to explore, imagine and be inspired by the discoveries shaping our world and the possibilities of tomorrow. From space exploration and artificial intelligence to ocean conservation, each screening offers an immersive experience that combines storytelling, science and conversation. All films begin at 6:30 p.m. Tickets are $35 per event, with the exception of the April 22 Earth Day screening, which begins at 7 p.m. and is $275. For tickets and additional information, visit https://glazerhall.org/event-category/science-films/. Artemis FAQs What is Artemis II? Artemis II is NASA’s first crewed mission of the Artemis program. Four astronauts will fly around the Moon (but not land), test the spacecraft with humans onboard, and return to Earth after about 10 days. Who’s going on Artemis II? The crew includes Reid Wiseman (Commander), Victor Glover (Pilot), Christina Koch (Mission Specialist), and Jeremy Hansen (Mission Specialist) Why was the launch delayed in February? NASA delayed the launch after NASA Completed a wet rehearsal which revealed a few issues, especially a liquid hydrogen leak. NASA’s philosophy is: “Fly only when ready.” Delays are normal, and expected, when testing brand-new space systems. Every delay means safer astronauts and better missions. What is a “wet dress rehearsal” Despite the name, no one gets soaked! A wet dress rehearsal is a full practice launch, including loading real fuel into the rocket, running the countdown, and testing systems and communications. Why is Artemis II such a big deal historically? When Artemis II flies, it will be: The first human mission beyond low Earth orbit since 1972 The first step toward long-term lunar exploration A test run for future Moon landings—and eventually Mars missions When will it launch? NASA is now targeting April 1 at the earliest, with several possible launch dates. In spaceflight, flexibility is part of the plan! To receive curated mission resources, stay informed with the latest updates, and receive commemorative stamps for their virtual guest passport after both liftoff and splashdown, sign up for NASA's Virtual Guest Program. To learn more about the Artemis II mission, visit the Cox Science Center and Aquarium or visit NASA's website.
